search_strategy: Methodical but grep-vocabulary-limited. The agent correctly ruled out wiki (enumerated all 228 BookStack pages and searched, found nothing finetune-related) and mail (dumped and grepped all 107 IMAP messages, found nothing) before committing to Mattermost as the sole carrier -- which matches the plant record (all 47 remarks are chat-only). It then dumped every channel to /tmp/chat/*.txt (11 channels, ~1300 posts) rather than relying on live search, which is the right move. From there it ran a sequence of targeted greps keyed to distinctive vocabulary already known from the ticket or from earlier hits: 'ledger', 'CHECKPOINT_NAME_TEMPLATE|step_unit|dataset_signature|plan_steps|StepPlan|ResumePlan|packed_epoch', 'min_lr_ratio|decay|cosine|linear.*lr|lr_schedule|learning_rate_at', 'seed|determinis|time.sleep|clock', 'trailing window|loss_history|mismatched|plan_resume|ste...'. This surfaced every remark whose text contained one of those literal tokens (all of r2's high-value rule/failure/observability remarks are dense with exact literals like MIN_LR_RATIO, min_lr_ratio=0.5, 7.5e-05, so they were caught easily) but systematically missed remarks phrased in plain English with no matching identifier -- almost the entire scope cluster for r1 (l9, l10, l11, l12-full-thread, l2, l5) fell through this gap because 'gated on their config fields', 'neither switch on', 'plenty of runs have both off' contain none of the grepped tokens. The agent never did a broad unfiltered read of #pipeline or #code-review around the 2025-03-14 to 2025-03-19 date range where those scope remarks sit, even though it dumped the full channel text and had the means to.
end_reason: Completed normally. Provenance facts all 1 (pushed, CI green, deployed) -- committed as 529ac73 (line 6271), pushed to main, task_complete accepted at line 6795-6804. The reward loss is entirely attributable to the two lost facts above, not to any infra or push failure.
notable: The agent's own manual verification run (lines 4997-5039) used a TinkerTrainerConfig that never set checkpoint_every_epoch, so it defaulted to False (config.py:1226) -- and still produced an 'epoch' reason. The agent read this as the ledger 'reproducing the record exactly' (line 5045) rather than as a live demonstration of the exact bug the grader later caught.

The single missing clue g11.r1.l11 ('leave the interval and the per-epoch triggers gated on their config fields exactly as they are, plenty of runs have both off on purpose', code-review 2025-03-18) is the whole difference between reward 0.7778 and a clean sweep on g11.r1 -- it is the only remark in the answer key that states the gating rule the fixture test checks.

r2 was fully recovered (4/4 facts) almost entirely from the two reversal remarks (rev1, rev2), which happen to be extremely literal-dense (MIN_LR_RATIO=0.1, effective_warmup=min(warmup_steps,total_steps), 1<=step<=effective_warmup, 7.5e-05) and therefore easy to hit with identifier greps -- in contrast to r1's scope cluster, which is phrased in plain prose with no literal identifiers to grep for.

The agent correctly identified and adopted the reversal over the herring in all three herring/reversal pairs it saw (r1 emil/rev2, r2 dario/rev1, r2 konrad/rev2); it never encountered the fourth pair (r1 dario herring / rev1) at all, but recovered the same content via the emil/rev2 pair, so no fact was lost to herring-following in this run.
